Claim 26 (Currently amended): A non-transitory machine readable medium storing a program which when executed by at least one processing unit analyzes a document, the program comprising sets of instructions for: receiving a document that comprises a plurality of primitive graphic elements defined separately within the document, the document having a drawing order that indicates the order in which the primitive graphic elements are drawn when the document is displayed; calculating a first value for a first primitive graphic element and a second primitive graphic element that is subsequent to the first in the drawing order, wherein the first value is calculated based on __spatial relationships between the first and second primitive graphic elements including at least one of relative positioning, overlap characteristics, or containment relationships__; and based on the comparison of the first value to other values calculated for additional primitive graphic elements that are subsequent in the drawing order, defining a single structural graphic element within the document from the first and second primitive graphic elements __only when the first value satisfies a predetermined threshold condition that distinguishes the first and second primitive graphic elements from other primitive graphic elements in the document__.

Claim 27 (Currently amended): The non-transitory machine readable medium of claim 26, wherein the first value is __derived from__ a size value __in combination with spatial relationship analysis__.

Claim 28 (Currently amended): The non-transitory machine readable medium of claim 26, wherein the first value represents __a normalized metric based on__ a size of a smallest bounding box that encompasses the first and second primitive graphic elements __and the spatial proximity between the first and second primitive graphic elements__.

Claim 31 (Currently amended): The non-transitory machine readable medium of claim 26, wherein the set of instructions for calculating comprises a set of instructions for calculating a different value for each pair of primitive graphic elements subsequent in the drawing order, wherein the set of instructions for defining the single structural graphic element comprises sets of instructions for: using the calculated values for pairs of primitive graphic elements to identify clusters of primitive graphic elements as candidates for joining as compound graphic elements; __identifying sequences of primitive graphic elements within a cluster whose bounding boxes intersect and whose spatial relationships satisfy the predetermined threshold condition__; and joining the sequences as single graphic elements.

Claim 32 (Currently amended): A non-transitory machine readable medium storing a program which when executed by at least one processing unit analyzes a document, the program comprising sets of instructions for: receiving a document that comprises a plurality of primitive graphic elements defined separately within the document; based on values calculated for pairs of primitive graphic elements __that incorporate spatial relationship analysis including relative positioning and overlap characteristics__, defining a set of successive primitive graphic elements as a candidate compound graphic element; using bounds of the primitive graphic elements in the cluster to identify one or more subsets of primitive graphic elements within the set __based on intersection and containment relationships__; and defining each particular subset having more than one primitive graphic element as a single structural graphic element within the document, the structure graphic element comprising the primitive graphic elements in the particular subset.

Claim 33 (Currently amended): The non-transitory machine readable medium of claim 32, wherein the set of instructions for defining the set of successive primitive graphic elements comprises performing cluster analysis on the calculated values __using spatial relationship metrics as clustering parameters__.

Claim 34 (Currently amended): The non-transitory machine readable medium of claim 32, wherein the set of instructions for using bounds of the primitive graphic elements in the cluster to identify one or more subsets of primitive graphic elements comprises sets of instructions for: selecting a first graphic element in the cluster and assigning the graphic element to a new sub-cluster; assigning a second graphic element in the cluster to the sub-cluster when a bounding box of the second graphic element overlaps a bounding box of the sub-cluster __and satisfies a spatial proximity criterion__.

Claim 35 (Currently amended): The non-transitory machine readable medium of claim 34, wherein the set of instructions for using bounds of the primitive graphic elements in the cluster to identify one or more subsets of primitive graphic elements further comprises a set of instructions for assigning a third graphic element to a second sub-cluster when a bounding box of the third graphic element does not overlap the bounding box of the sub-cluster __and fails to satisfy the spatial proximity criterion__.

Claim 36 (Previously presented): The non-transitory machine readable medium of claim 34, wherein the bounding box of the sub-cluster is an intersection of the bounding boxes of all primitive graphic elements already in the sub-cluster.

Claim 37 (Currently amended): A method for analyzing a document, the method comprising: receiving a document that comprises a plurality of primitive graphic elements defined separately within the document, the document having a drawing order that indicates the order in which the primitive graphic elements are drawn when the document is displayed; calculating a first value for a first primitive graphic element and a second primitive graphic element that is subsequent to the first in the drawing order, wherein the first value is calculated based on __spatial relationships between the first and second primitive graphic elements including at least one of relative positioning, overlap characteristics, or containment relationships__; and based on the comparison of the first value to other values calculated for additional primitive graphic elements that are subsequent in the drawing order, defining a single structural graphic element within the document from the first and second primitive graphic elements __only when the first value satisfies a predetermined threshold condition that distinguishes the first and second primitive graphic elements from other primitive graphic elements in the document__.

Claim 38 (Currently amended): The method of claim 37, wherein the first value represents __a normalized metric based on__ a size of a smallest bounding box that encompasses the first and second primitive graphic elements __and the spatial proximity between the first and second primitive graphic elements__.

Claim 39 (Previously presented): The method of claim 38, wherein the size of the smallest bounding box is calculated as a sum of a width and height of the bounding box divided by a sum of a width and height of a page containing the primitive graphic elements.

Claim 40 (Previously presented): The method of claim 38, wherein the size of the smallest bounding box is calculated as an area of the bounding box divided by an area of a page containing the primitive graphic elements.

Claim 41 (Currently amended): The method of claim 37, wherein the calculating comprises calculating a different value for each pair of primitive graphic elements subsequent in the drawing order, wherein defining the single structural graphic element comprises: using the calculated values for pairs of primitive graphic elements to identify clusters of primitive graphic elements as candidates for joining as compound graphic elements; and __identifying sequences of primitive graphic elements within a cluster whose bounding boxes intersect and whose spatial relationships satisfy the predetermined threshold condition__; and joining the sequences as single graphic elements.

Claim 42 (Currently amended): An apparatus comprising: a set of processing units; and a machine readable medium storing a program which when executed by at least one processing unit analyzes a document, the program comprising sets of instructions for: receiving a document that comprises a plurality of primitive graphic elements defined separately within the document; based on values calculated for pairs of primitive graphic elements __that incorporate spatial relationship analysis including relative positioning and overlap characteristics__, defining a set of successive primitive graphic elements as a candidate compound graphic element; using bounds of the primitive graphic elements in the cluster to identify one or more subsets of primitive graphic elements within the set __based on intersection and containment relationships__; and defining each particular subset having more than one primitive graphic element as a single structural graphic element within the document, the structure graphic element comprising the primitive graphic elements in the particular subset.

Claim 43 (Currently amended): The apparatus of claim 42, wherein the set of instructions for using bounds of the primitive graphic elements in the cluster to identify one or more subsets of primitive graphic elements comprises sets of instructions for: selecting a first graphic element in the cluster and assigning the graphic element to a new sub-cluster; assigning a second graphic element in the cluster to the sub-cluster when a bounding box of the second graphic element overlaps a bounding box of the sub-cluster __and satisfies a spatial proximity criterion__.

Claim 44 (Currently amended): The apparatus of claim 43, wherein the set of instructions for using bounds of the primitive graphic elements in the cluster to identify one or more subsets of primitive graphic elements further comprises a set of instructions for assigning a third graphic element to a second sub-cluster when a bounding box of the third graphic element does not overlap the bounding box of the sub-cluster __and fails to satisfy the spatial proximity criterion__.

Claim 45 (Previously presented): The apparatus of claim 43, wherein the bounding box of the sub-cluster is an intersection of the bounding boxes of all primitive graphic elements already in the sub-cluster.

Claim 46 (Previously presented): The apparatus of claim 42, wherein the document comprises an unstructured vector graphics document.
